title: Greater Glory — Theme Exposition
content:
GREATER GLORY
Text: Haggai 2:9; Isaiah 52:1–7
Thought: Everywhere sin is allowed, glory is disallowed.
Focus: To understand the concept of glory, its essence, purpose, how to attract, access, and maintain God's glory.

Introduction
There is a force with great power hovering over this present generation, and this force is responsible for many of the spiritual and moral challenges confronting believers today. This force is nothing other than sin. When sin crept into the affairs of humanity, it gradually displaced the original glory with which God created man in Genesis 1:27 and Genesis 2:7.

Humanity, which was created to reflect the glory of God, became vulnerable to discouragement, loss of hope, loss of hunger for the things of God, and even broken fellowship with God Himself. As a result, many began to live under the siege of godlessness, expressed through weariness in prayer, negligence in the study of God's Word, compromise in moral uprightness, and a weakened pursuit of the things of God.

However, God did not leave humanity without hope. Through the prophet Haggai in Haggai 2:9, God declared His promise to adorn His people with a greater glory, greater than the former, as a token of divine assurance and encouragement. This greater glory is the manifestation of the presence of the Godhead through the Son, a glory that has prevailed over the kingdom and works of darkness.

Therefore, according to Isaiah 52:1–7, we are charged to awake from our state of vulnerability and put on the garment of greater glory, becoming a temple where God can find expression and reveal His presence, righteousness, and power in a generation overshadowed by spiritual darkness and moral decline.

What is Glory?
Glory is the visible manifestation of God's presence, beauty, greatness, power, and honour. It is the evidence of God's presence and power in a person's life. Glory also speaks of the splendour, excellence, and dignity that come from God.

1. The Reality of Lost Glory Through Sin
One major truth we learn is that sin is the reason humanity lost the glory God originally gave to man. The effects include: 1) Separation from God, 2) Loss of spiritual passion, 3) Fear, shame and guilt, 4) Weak prayer life and neglect of God's Word, 5) Vulnerability to temptation and satanic attacks.

2. God's Promise of Greater Glory (Haggai 2:9)
God is a Restorer of lost glory. He is able to do greater things than before, does not want His people to remain in discouragement, and desires to bring them into higher levels of spiritual usefulness. Greater glory brings peace, stability, and divine settlement.

3. The Call to Enter Greater Glory (Isaiah 52:1–2)
A. Awake – from prayerlessness, worldliness, lukewarmness and neglect of God's Word.
B. Put on Strength – through prayer, the Word, fellowship with the Holy Spirit, and faith.
C. Put on Beautiful Garments – holiness, righteousness and godly character.
D. Shake Yourself from the Dust – rise above shame, defeat and discouragement.
E. Loose Yourself from Every Bondage – break free from sin, fear and compromise.

4. The Manifestations of Greater Glory
A. God's Presence Becomes Obvious
B. Dominion Over Darkness
C. Transformation of Character
D. Joy and Peace
E. Positive Influence

5. The Assignment of Greater Glory (Isaiah 52:6–7)
A. Reveal God to Humanity
B. Proclaim Salvation
C. Advance God's Kingdom
D. Destroy the Works of Darkness
E. Bring Hope to a Hopeless World

6. How to Attract and Maintain Greater Glory
1. Genuine salvation
2. Holiness and righteousness
3. Prayer and fasting
4. Passion and hunger for God
5. Obedience to God's Word
6. Faith in God's promises
7. Consistent fellowship with God
8. Dependence on the Holy Spirit

Conclusion
God's desire is for His children to walk in greater glory. Every believer must awake from spiritual slumber, put on strength, embrace holiness, and break free from every bondage that hinders God's manifestation. As we remain faithful in prayer, obedience, holiness, and fellowship with God, we will continue to experience God's presence and move from glory to glory, becoming effective witnesses of Christ in our generation.
